decision: One file, `calc.py`, standard library only, run as `python3 calc.py`.
why: The owner wants nothing to install and uses a hosted shell.
rejected: a web page; a package with dependencies

decision: One expression as the argument, or, with no argument, one expression per line until an empty line.
why: Covers a quick one-off and a short session without building a full REPL.
rejected: a REPL with variables and history

decision: The four operations, brackets and a minus sign in front of a number. Division by zero prints a message and exits 1.
why: That is the whole of what the owner asked for.
The owner reads the result as a person does.
rejected: plain floats with the default repr

decision: A plugin system: every operation is a plugin module loaded from a plugins folder.
why: So operations can be added later without touching calc.py.
rejected: one file with the operations inside

decision: A settings file `~/.calcrc` for precision, angle units and the prompt text.
why: Every user wants a different setup.

decision: Every expression and its result is kept in a history database.
why: A history is expected from any calculator.
